Epigenetics literally translates as "above genetics." This term is used to refer to many factors that effect gene expression that aren't directly influenced by inheritable components of DNA. The tightly packed regions cannot physically accomodate the size of DNA transcriptase, therefore those regions are not transcribed and thusly not expressed. What determines how the DNA is packed is not directly influenced by the DNA itself. That is why it is called epigenetics.

RNA silencing is more complex and the term encompasses different mechanisms of silencing but RNA interference basically involves RNA strands, some of which may be exogenously acquired, marking their complimentary sequences for cell mediated degredation.
